From 4bb7f6c2781e46fc5bd00475a66df2ea30ef330d Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Rafael J. Wysocki" <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Date: Thu, 13 Oct 2022 14:50:28 +0200
Subject: [PATCH] thermal: intel_powerclamp: Use first online CPU as
 control_cpu

Commit 68b99e94a4a2 ("thermal: intel_powerclamp: Use get_cpu() instead
of smp_processor_id() to avoid crash") fixed an issue related to using
smp_processor_id() in preemptible context by replacing it with a pair
of get_cpu()/put_cpu(), but what is needed there really is any online
CPU and not necessarily the one currently running the code.  Arguably,
getting the one that's running the code in there is confusing.

For this reason, simply give the control CPU role to the first online
one which automatically will be CPU0 if it is online, so one check
can be dropped from the code for an added benefit.

Link: https://lore.kernel.org/linux-pm/20221011113646.GA12080@duo.ucw.cz/
Fixes: 68b99e94a4a2 ("thermal: intel_powerclamp: Use get_cpu() instead of smp_processor_id() to avoid crash")
Signed-off-by: Rafael J. Wysocki <rafael.j.wysocki@intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Chen Yu <yu.c.chen@intel.com>

diff --git a/drivers/thermal/intel/intel_powerclamp.c b/drivers/thermal/intel/intel_powerclamp.c
index 2a5570b9799a..b80e25ec1261 100644
--- a/drivers/thermal/intel/intel_powerclamp.c
+++ b/drivers/thermal/intel/intel_powerclamp.c
@@ -516,11 +516,7 @@ static int start_power_clamp(void)
 	cpus_read_lock();
 
 	/* prefer BSP */
-	control_cpu = 0;
-	if (!cpu_online(control_cpu)) {
-		control_cpu = get_cpu();
-		put_cpu();
-	}
+	control_cpu = cpumask_first(cpu_online_mask);
 
 	clamping = true;
 	schedule_delayed_work(&poll_pkg_cstate_work, 0);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/thermal/intel/intel_powerclamp.c`**
- The code that previously set `control_cpu` to `0` and checked if it was online has been removed.
- Instead, `control_cpu` is now assigned the value of the first online CPU using `cpumask_first(cpu_online_mask)`. This change simplifies the logic by directly selecting the first available online CPU.

### Relationships
- The modification addresses a previous bug fix (commit 68b99e94a4a2) that replaced `smp_processor_id()` with `get_cpu()` to avoid crashes in preemptible contexts. The current patch refines this approach by selecting any online CPU instead of the one currently executing the code, which is deemed less confusing and more efficient. This change also eliminates an unnecessary check for the online status of CPU0, streamlining the code further.

Root cause:
The bug was caused by using `smp_processor_id()` in a preemptible context, which can lead to crashes due to the potential for context switches. This method retrieves the ID of the currently executing CPU, which is not safe in scenarios where the CPU may be preempted. The fix initially implemented replaced this with `get_cpu()` and `put_cpu()`, but it was determined that any online CPU could be used instead, simplifying the logic and avoiding confusion.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
control_cpu = 0;
if (!cpu_online(control_cpu)) {
    control_cpu = get_cpu();
    put_cpu();
}
```
Reason:
The use of `smp_processor_id()` (which was replaced by `get_cpu()` and `put_cpu()`) retrieves the ID of the currently executing CPU, which can lead to crashes in a preemptible context due to potential context switches. This approach is confusing as it assumes the currently running CPU is the best choice for control, which is not necessarily true.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
control_cpu = cpumask_first(cpu_online_mask);
```
Reason:
This change assigns the control CPU to the first online CPU instead of the currently executing one. This simplifies the logic and avoids the risks associated with preemption, ensuring that any online CPU can be used safely without the confusion of relying on the currently executing CPU.
